column11: JUDGEMENT: no Phase 3 is registered. GALILEO (NCT06185764) completes 2027-02-02 and Vertex will share multiple ascending dose results in H2 2026 (8-K exhibit 99.1, 0000875320-26-000256), so a registrational study starts in 2027 at the earliest. The DM1 analogue is del-desiran's HARBOR (NCT06411288): Phase 3 start 2024-05-30 to primary completion 2026-07-23, 2.15 years, topline on 2026-09-08 (Novartis release). That puts VX-670's primary completion in late 2029. A BLA filed around the end of 2029 under priority review acts eight months later, as the AOC 1044 seed dates del-zota's (submitted 2026-06-25, action by about 2027-02-25), so approval in H2 2030 and a first full year of 2031
column12: HARBOR missed its primary endpoint, video hand opening time (Novartis release, 2026-09-08). A registrational VX-670 trial may need to be larger or longer as a result, which would make 2031 early

column11: Two factors multiplied. (1) Label, 0.902588: GALILEO (NCT06185764) enrols ages 18 to 64 with onset after age one, so the likely label is adults. In 8,541 US patients with myotonic dystrophy in claims (Howe SJ et al., Orphanet J Rare Dis 2022;17:79, Table 1), 2,003 were 18 to 39 and 5,706 were 40 or older: 7,709 / 8,541 = 0.902588. (2) Acceptance, 0.284428, FITTED to Skyclarys, the first therapy for a rare inherited neuromuscular disease: the engine has no gate on who ever takes a drug, so the share of eligible patients the analogue holds is carried here. US Skyclarys revenue was $301.1mm in 2024 and $310.6mm in 2025 (Biogen FY2025 10-K, 0000875045-26-000013, product revenue table), which at a net of $267,251 (the price and gross-to-net rows) is 1,127 and 1,162 patients, 25.04% and 25.83% of Reata's addressable US population at launch of about 4,500 (Drug Discovery & Development, 2023-03-03; Biogen's Reata acquisition release, 8-K exhibit 99.1 0001193125-23-196808, puts diagnosed US patients at about 5,000). Fitted jointly with penetration_peak_pct on the engine's own flow (closed pool, stopping 8.9% a year, the curve below) to reproduce both years exactly: acceptance 0.284428 and capture 0.886181 of the willing untreated pool a year. 0.902588 x 0.284428 = 0.256721, about 8,134 US adults
column12: JUDGEMENT: a multiple of 1.0 on Skyclarys, whose US revenue went flat from 2024 to 2025, the plateau the acceptance share reads. Case for lower: DM1 is more variable than Friedreich ataxia and many clinically apparent adults have mild disease; GALILEO also requires at least 100 CTG repeats, a filter no US count applies; an infusion asks more of a patient than a capsule; and del-desiran missed its Phase 3 primary endpoint. Case for higher: DM1 has no approved therapy, and Vertex's own 110,000 US and Europe estimate is larger than this pool with the ex-US multiple (50,449)

derived: Vertex generated $12,074mm of free cash flow on $49,396mm of revenue over the five years to 2025, a 24.44% margin, against the 33.0% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Five years rather than three because operating cash flow was negative $493mm in 2024 on the Alpine acquisition, which takes a three-year window to 17.5% and lets one deal set the rate. Solved so the modelled book reproduces the margin rather than taken off a single line. Restated before interest: VRTX paid $195mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2021 to 2025, 0.39% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 10.33% to 9.94%. Restated at replacement capex: VRTX spent $1,375mm on plant over 2021 to 2025 against $758mm of plant depreciation, 1.25% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 9.94% to 8.47%. Restated without one-off cash: VRTX's free cash flow over 2021 to 2025 carried $6,517mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately. None recurs, so the charge falls from 8.47% to 0.00%. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 39.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2021 to 2025 supports 43.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -4.72%. It was held at nil, but VRTX books $20mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0000875320-26-000056), 0.17% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -0.17%. Restated without working capital build: over 2021 to 2025 VRTX's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,164mm, inventories up $1,594mm, payables up $288mm, a working capital build of $2,470mm, 5.00% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -0.17% where the filed figures rebuild it at -4.72%, and stays there.
